description:
Native Windows music player for the YouTube Music catalogue, with a local library, queue, autoplay, and audio caching.

Auricle is a native desktop music player for Windows, built with Rust and the
Slint UI toolkit. Search the YouTube Music catalogue, organize your local
library, and keep listening without Electron or an embedded web view.

Features:
- Search songs, albums, artists, and playlists with suggestions and mixed previews.
- Browse artist and album pages, save albums and playlists, and follow artists locally.
- Explore artist and album credits and manage the queue through right-click menus.
- Play, pause, seek, adjust volume, and continue listening with queue and autoplay controls.
- Keep liked songs and listening history on your device.
- Reuse recently played audio with a size-limited local cache, set to 500 MB by default.
- Minimize to the Windows system tray while playback continues.

Auricle does not bundle yt-dlp, ffmpeg or Deno. Audio extraction relies on
yt-dlp, some cache operations use ffmpeg, and yt-dlp can use Deno as a
JavaScript runtime. On first run, an optional add-on step offers to download
these tools from their official GitHub releases into a per-user application
directory. You can also install them yourself and make them available on PATH.
Once yt-dlp is installed, Auricle updates it automatically in the background
at most once a week (and once per session if playback fails because it is out
of date). Browser cookies are never used by default; only if you turn on
"Use browser cookies for YouTube" in Settings and accept the explanation does
yt-dlp load cookies from Edge, Chrome or Firefox and send the YouTube ones to
YouTube over verified HTTPS. You can turn it off at any time.

Auricle has no accounts, telemetry or analytics. It keeps a local diagnostic
log and offers a user-initiated "Report a problem" GitHub issue; see the
privacy policy for what is stored locally and what is sent to YouTube, Google
and GitHub.

This is an early Windows release. Streaming depends on external services and
optional add-ons, and availability and regional restrictions can vary.
Auricle is not affiliated with YouTube or Google.

Auricle 0.1.7 restores search, artwork and streaming after recent YouTube
changes: YouTube Music requests work again, stream links are used only once
YouTube makes them available, and songs that are not cached start in about
three seconds again. Privacy behaviour is unchanged from 0.1.6: browser cookies
stay strictly opt-in with an in-app consent dialog, TLS certificate verification
stays on for all yt-dlp requests, and the diagnostic log stays local unless you
choose "Report a problem".

The native Rust and Slint player includes catalogue search, a local library,
queue and autoplay controls, listening history, audio caching, and system tray playback.

Streaming depends on external services and optional, separately installed
yt-dlp, ffmpeg and Deno add-ons. These tools are not bundled with Auricle.
